description: Exobiology: genus, species, biome predictions, sample values

entries.content: Exobiology samples are collected using the Genetic Sampler tool. Three samples from distinct colonies of the same species are required to complete analysis. Samples must be collected from colonies separated by a minimum distance (the Colonial Range), which is species-specific. The journal records each sample via the ScanOrganic event with ScanType values of Log, Sample, and Analyse.

entries.topic: Signal Counts and Genera Are Journal Facts, Not Predictions
entries.content: After a Detailed Surface Scanner map, Elite reports the number of biological signals on a body in SAASignalsFound.Signals[] with Type '$SAA_SignalType_Biological;' and a Count. In Odyssey the same event also carries a Genuses[] array naming which genera are present. Both are observed facts and must be surfaced as such. Only the species within a genus, and the credit value of a sample, require prediction or reference estimation. A tool that predicts a signal count when the journal already reported one is discarding a fact in favour of a guess.
entries._justification: Phase 13 exobiology slice. Records the fact/prediction boundary so future work reads SAASignalsFound before reaching for a condition matcher.

entries.topic: Species Suggestions from Independent Journal Evidence
entries.content: Frontier has never published where biological organisms can occur, so OmniCOVAS does not claim to know the rules. What it holds instead is evidence: an original aggregate of confirmed sightings compiled from Frontier journal events (Scan, ScanOrganic, CodexEntry and SAASignalsFound) that commanders relayed through EDDN and that EDGalaxyData archived. For each of 91 species it records how many distinct bodies it was confirmed on, grouped by the planet class, atmosphere and 10 K surface-temperature band the game recorded for those bodies. It contains no commander names, uploader identifiers, system or body identifiers, or raw messages, and no occurrence content from third-party prediction tables. The game's own reports always come first. Biological signal counts from FSSBodySignals and SAASignalsFound, and the genera SAASignalsFound names after a surface map, are facts and are never predicted over. Before genera are named, OmniCOVAS shows preliminary genus suggestions: genera confirmed on bodies with the same recorded planet class and atmosphere, strongest first. Once a genus is named, every species of that genus stays a candidate. They are ranked by confirmed sightings at a similar temperature, then on the same planet class and atmosphere, then anywhere; the strongest three lead and the rest stay available. In out-of-period checks on real discoveries the confirmed species was among the top three suggestions about 99% of the time, which measures how well real finds were identified, not the chance of finding a species on a given planet. Counts are not spawn probabilities and never rule a species out: a species seldom or never seen under some conditions in the sample may still occur there. Three species (Concha Biconcavis, Fonticulua Fluctus and Radicoida Unica) were confirmed on fewer than ten bodies and carry a sparse-evidence warning. Suggestions are species-level; colour variants are shown only when ScanOrganic confirms them. A species the Commander logs with ScanOrganic is shown as confirmed and replaces any suggestion for its genus on that body. The machine source is omnicovas/data/exobiology_journal_evidence_v1.json; this entry describes how it is used, not the data itself.
entries.source: Original OmniCOVAS aggregate of positive sightings from Frontier Elite Dangerous journal events relayed by the Elite Dangerous Data Network (EDDN) and archived by EDGalaxyData (daily archives 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-03), validated against separate 2026-09-20 and 2026-10-20 archives. Field meanings follow Frontier's Player Journal v37. No EDMC-BioScan, Canonn, Deep Space Network or other third-party occurrence rules were used. Not Frontier-published.
entries._justification: FU-021 replaced the legacy community-derived occurrence ruleset, whose distribution was not cleared, with independently compiled journal evidence. Rewritten to describe evidence ranking instead of rule branches, and to drop the Rule Sentinel, which only existed to suspend legacy rules. Confidence stays medium: the evidence covers a short archive window, reflects where commanders chose to explore, and is sparse for three species.

entries.content: Exobiology payouts vary enormously by genus and species, from roughly 1 million credits for common Bacterium variants to roughly 19-20 million for the highest-value species such as Stratum Tectonicas. A first-logged bonus (historically an additional multiple of base value) applies when the Commander is the first to register that species. Actual credits received are always reported by the journal in SellOrganicData BioData[] Value and Bonus fields, and those observed values must always take precedence over any reference figure. Reference values are for pre-sale expectation only, change with balance patches, and must never be added to a figure describing money already received.
entries.source: community value tables and in-game observation; not Frontier-published
entries._justification: Phase 13 exobiology value slice. Ranges only, never per-species precision, because the source does not support precision and a wrong exact figure reads as authoritative. SellOrganicData observed values outrank this entry wherever both exist.
